# Parameters

Every parameter openmobisim 0.1.0 assumes, at the value a `Scenario` uses (from `openmobisim.parameters()`). Every value is an uncalibrated default and can be overridden by name through the argument shown; a misspelt name is refused with the list of known ones. 251 parameters in 14 groups.

## `scenario`

Each overridden through its own argument.

| Name | Argument | Default | Unit | Meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `flow_level` | `flow_level` | 2 | level | How vehicles load the network: 0 free flow (no vehicle affects another), 2 the point queue (queues form at capacity but take no road space, so nothing spills back), 3 a spatial queue, 4 the full triangular fundamental diagram, with spillback, turn pockets and en-route rerouting. | A choice of model, not a calibrated value. |
| `flow_step_s` | `flow_step_s` | 300 | s | The loading's step at flow levels 2 to 4, in seconds: a bookkeeping boundary at which links forget what they no longer need; no vehicle's timing depends on it. | A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed. |
| `window` | `window` | 3 | h | The simulation window's length when `window` is not given: the run starts at the earliest departure, rounded down to the quarter hour, and stops this many hours later. Trips departing outside the window are left out with a `WindowWarning`; trips still under way at its end are unfinished. *(from the earliest departure (rounded down to the quarter hour))* | A setting: the starter cases' morning departures span three hours. |
| `default_weight` | `default_weight` | 1 | travellers | How many people one simulated traveller stands for, for a trip whose row gives no weight: 1 simulates everyone; more is faster and coarser. | A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed. |
| `master_seed` | `master_seed` | 0 | — | The one number every random stream starts from (who chooses again, which alternative a sampled choice model draws): the same seed reproduces a run. A whole number from 0 to 2^64 − 1. | A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed. |
| `choice_detour_limit` | `choice_detour_limit` | 0.5 | share | A traveller is offered a route only if its expected time, at the last loading's times (free flow at first), is at most this share above the best route's: 0.5 offers routes at most 50 % slower. 0 offers every route of the set. The best route is always offered; with mode choice the limit applies within each mode. | An assumption; no published source. |
| `choice_max_routes` | `choice_max_routes` | 5 | routes | The most routes a traveller is offered: the fastest at their departure among those within `choice_detour_limit`; 0 offers every route within the limit. A pair's set may hold more (`route_update` `max_routes`). | An assumption on the size of a consideration set: Prato (2009), Route choice modeling: past, present and future research directions, Journal of Choice Modelling 2(1) 65–100, https://doi.org/10.1016/S1755-5345(13)70005-8, reviews choice sets of a handful of routes. |
| `hub_group_m` | `hub_group_m` | 150 | m | How far a parking may be from a stop, in metres in a straight line, to share the stop's hub group in the outputs (`hub_group`); an argument of `Scenario.run`. A label: results do not depend on it, so it is not in the fingerprint. *(a label of the outputs (Scenario.run); not in the fingerprint)* | An assumption: a short walk across a station's forecourt. Uncalibrated. |

## `network`

Overridden through `network_options`.

| Name | Default | Unit | Meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bike_dedicated_km_h` | 18 | km/h | A bike's speed on a painted lane, cycle street or separate track, in km/h; never above the link's speed limit. | An assumption: 20 % above the mixed-traffic speed, for fewer stops and conflicts. On a Bologna street cyclists slowed about 20 % on a separated facility against 40 % in mixed traffic: Bernardi, Krizek and Rupi (2016), Journal of Transport and Land Use, https://jtlu.org/index.php/jtlu/article/view/715 |
| `bike_lane_cost_factor` | 1 | — | With `bike_cost="dedicated"`, multiplies the travel time of a bike link with a painted lane (or a cycle street) when bike routes are searched, against 1 on a separate track; 1 counts a lane as a track. | Uncalibrated. In Portland painted lanes were no more attractive than a quiet street while off-street paths were valued highly (Broach, Dill and Gliebe 2012, Transportation Research Part A 46(10) 1730–1740, https://ideas.repec.org/a/eee/transa/v46y2012i10p1730-1740.html); a value between 1 and `bike_mixed_cost_factor` is to be taken from such a model. |
| `bike_mixed_cost_factor` | 1.2 | — | With `bike_cost="dedicated"` (the default), multiplies the travel time of every bike link without a lane or track (ferries excepted) when bike routes are searched, so cyclists accept a detour to ride on dedicated infrastructure; the time ridden is unchanged. No effect with `bike_cost="time"`. | An assumption, a placeholder until a value is taken from a route choice model. Cyclists valued off-street paths highly in Portland (Broach, Dill and Gliebe 2012, Transportation Research Part A 46(10) 1730–1740, https://ideas.repec.org/a/eee/transa/v46y2012i10p1730-1740.html) and appeared indifferent to separate paths in Amsterdam's inner city (Ton, Cats, Duives and Hoogendoorn 2017, Transportation Research Record 2662 75–82, https://doi.org/10.3141/2662-09). |
| `bike_mixed_km_h` | 15 | km/h | A bike's speed in mixed traffic, stops included, in km/h; never above the link's speed limit. | About 15 km/h is the urban average in the Netherlands, stop time included: de Hartog, Boogaard, Nijland and Hoek, Environmental Health Perspectives, 2011, the authors' response in the correspondence on their 2010 paper, https://doi.org/10.1289/ehp.0901747. |
| `busway.free_flow_km_h` | 50 | km/h | Free-flow speed of a busway (buses only: `highway=busway`, or a road closed to other motor traffic but open to buses) where the data gives no `maxspeed`, in km/h; every speed is then multiplied by `free_flow_speed_factor`. A higher speed shortens free-flow times and, with capacity and jam density, changes the backward wave speed. | An assumption: a secondary road's speed, buses running at urban arterial speeds. |
| `busway.jam_density_veh_km_lane` | 130 | veh/km per lane | Jam density of a busway (buses only: `highway=busway`, or a road closed to other motor traffic but open to buses): vehicles (PCU) per km and lane at a standstill, so how many vehicles a link stores. With the free-flow speed v and capacity q it sets the backward wave speed, w = q / (k_j − q/v). Multiplied by `jam_density_factor`. | An assumption: a secondary road's row. |
| `busway.lanes` | 1 | count | Lanes per direction of a busway (buses only: `highway=busway`, or a road closed to other motor traffic but open to buses) where the data gives no lane count. Capacity and storage (jam density) are per lane, so both scale with it; turn pockets need two lanes or more. | An assumption: a secondary road's row. |
| `busway.saturation_flow_veh_h_lane` | 1800 | veh/h per lane | Capacity per lane of a busway (buses only: `highway=busway`, or a road closed to other motor traffic but open to buses), in vehicles (PCU) per hour, where the data states no capacity; times the lanes it is the link's capacity, then multiplied by `capacity_factor`. At a signal it is capped by the speed band (`street_30`, `street_50`, `street_70`). | An assumption: a secondary road's row. |
| `capacity_factor` | 1 | — | Multiplies every road link's capacity, including a capacity the data states, after the signal speed bands' cap. | A calibration factor; 1 leaves the shipped table unchanged. |
| `control_delay_factor` | 1 | — | Multiplies the constant control delay added to the free-flow time of every link that ends at a signal. | A calibration factor; 1 leaves the shipped table unchanged. |
| `cycleway.free_flow_km_h` | 30 | km/h | Not read by any computation: links of this class have static speeds on the walk or bike layer (`walk_km_h`, `bike_mixed_km_h`, `bike_dedicated_km_h`, `ferry_km_h`). The row only keeps the table complete. | Not used; filled with the residential row. |
| `cycleway.jam_density_veh_km_lane` | 140 | veh/km per lane | Not read by any computation: links of this class have static speeds on the walk or bike layer (`walk_km_h`, `bike_mixed_km_h`, `bike_dedicated_km_h`, `ferry_km_h`). The row only keeps the table complete. | Not used; filled with the residential row. |

## `loading`

Overridden through `loading_options`.

| Name | Default | Unit | Meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `priority` | 0 | 0 or 1 | 1 turns on priority at unsignalised merges: a vehicle gives way to the front vehicle of an approach of higher road class (or of the same class and at least 1.5 times the capacity) bound for the same link, and a departing vehicle gives way to every approach. 0 or 1. | openmobisim's own remedy for loops of links that lock (uncalibrated). Off by default: with one first-in-first-out queue per link, a vehicle giving way holds up everything behind it. |
| `reroute` | 1 | 0 or 1 | 1 turns on en-route rerouting: a vehicle blocked at the front of its link for `reroute_after_s` re-routes from where it is. 0 or 1. Unsaid, it is on at flow levels 3 and 4 and off at level 2, where nothing waits for room. *(on at flow_level 3 and 4; off at 2 unless asked for (1))* | openmobisim's own remedy for loops of links that lock (uncalibrated): drivers who change course escape a locked loop. |
| `reroute_after_s` | 300 | s | How long a vehicle waits, blocked at the front of its link, before it re-routes, in seconds. | Uncalibrated; no observed diversion delay was found. MATSim's stuck time defaults to 30 s (Mersini and Ziemke, MATSim User Meeting 2025, slide 6, https://matsim.org/conferences/mum2025/presentations/mersini.pdf); Olmos et al. (2018), PNAS 115(50) 12654–12661, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6294880, let a vehicle stopped about two minutes re-route. |
| `reroute_max` | 3 | count | The most times one trip re-routes. | An assumption: three, to keep a vehicle from wandering. |
| `reroute_min_gain` | 0.1 | — | How much faster the new route must be than the rest of the current one, by the costs the vehicle sees, as a share, for a vehicle to re-route. | Uncalibrated. A relative threshold of this kind is the indifference band of boundedly rational route switching (Mahmassani and Jayakrishnan 1991, Transportation Research Part A 25(5) 293–307, https://doi.org/10.1016/0191-2607(91)90145-G); no observed value was taken from it. |
| `pocket_length_m` | 50 | m | Turn pockets on approaches of two lanes or more, in metres per lane, split among the approach's movements: a vehicle passes those ahead of it that wait for another movement, as long as they fit in their pockets. 0 turns pockets off (every link one first-in-first-out queue). | An assumption: design guides size a bay from its expected queue, so no single length was found. |

## `modes`

Overridden through `mode_options`.

| Name | Default | Unit | Meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `walk_max_s` | 1800 | s | The longest walk, in seconds, that mode choice offers to a trip choosing its mode; a trip whose mode is given walks at any length. A traveller class may give its own. | Uncalibrated: a 30-minute cut-off for a whole trip on foot. England's average walking trip took 18 minutes in 2022 (Department for Transport, Walking factsheet 2022, https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/64e71a3d20ae89000df26d2b/walking-factsheet-2022.pdf). |
| `bike_max_s` | 3600 | s | The longest ride, in seconds, that mode choice offers as a bike alternative to a trip choosing its mode; a trip whose mode is given rides at any length. A traveller class may give its own. | Uncalibrated: 60 minutes. About 80 % of Dutch bicycle trips are under 5 km (KiM, Cycling facts: new insights, 2020, https://english.kimnet.nl/documents/2020/11/03/cycling-facts-new-insights); the limit keeps the longer ones, e-bikes' among them. |
| `fallback_car` | 0 | 0 or 1 | 1: a trip left with no alternative at all (no mode it may use reaches its destination within the limits) travels by car instead, counted and reported apart; for a traveller without a car the car stands for a lift or a taxi. 0 leaves such trips unsimulated. 0 or 1. | An assumption; no published source. |
| `car_access_s` | 120 | s | The time a car trip takes before its drive — reaching the car and setting off — in seconds: added to a car alternative's door-to-door time and its walk in mode choice, and to the drive to a park-and-ride car park. 0 switches it off. | Uncalibrated: 120 s, an assumption with no published source. |
| `car_egress_s` | 180 | s | The time a car trip takes after its drive — finding a place and walking from it — in seconds: added to a car alternative's door-to-door time and its parking time in mode choice; a park-and-ride drive pays its car park's own time instead. 0 switches it off. | Uncalibrated: 180 s, an assumption. Cruising for parking alone averaged 8 minutes in sixteen downtown studies (Shoup 2006, Cruising for parking, Transport Policy 13(6), 479–486, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tranpol.2006.05.005), far above a city-wide mean that counts home and workplace parking. |
| `car_snap_motorway_m` | 50 | m | How close to a motorway-only node a trip's end must lie to join the roads there, in metres. A trip's end snaps to the nearest street node (one with a road a car can enter from; motorways, trunk roads and their ramps are not), unless it lies within this distance of a node that has only such roads, which it then takes. Read by every car trip. 0 sends every trip to a street; inf takes the nearest drivable node of any class. | Uncalibrated: 50 m, an assumption (a through trip placed on its motorway node lies at 0 m; an address is never within 50 m of a carriageway's node). No published source. |

## `transit`

Overridden through `transit_options`.

| Name | Default | Unit | Meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `board_slack_s` | 60 | s | How long before a vehicle leaves a passenger must be at the stop to board it, in seconds, at every boarding (a whole number). | An assumption: one minute to reach the platform and the door. Routing engines differ: OpenTripPlanner's boardSlack defaults to 0 (https://docs.opentripplanner.org/en/latest/RouteRequest/). |
| `max_rides` | 8 | count | The most vehicles one journey takes (eight rides is seven changes). | A resource limit, not behaviour: far beyond the journeys anyone makes in a city. |
| `access_walk_max_s` | 1800 | s | The longest walk from an origin to a stop, or from a stop to a destination, in seconds (1 800 s is 2.4 km at walking speed): a choice-set limit, not a preference, since the choice model weighs the minutes walked. A traveller class may give its own. | An assumption. In Montréal the 85th percentile of the walk to a stop is about 524 m for buses and 1 259 m for commuter rail (El-Geneidy et al. 2014, Transportation 41(1) 193–210, https://ideas.repec.org/a/kap/transp/v41y2014i1p193-210.html): the limit leaves room for the few who walk further. |
| `journey_max_s` | 7200 | s | The longest a journey with transit may take door to door, in seconds, to be offered: a longer one is no alternative. A choice-set limit, not a preference. | An assumption: two hours is more than a city's morning trip by transit takes. |
| `transfer_walk_max_s` | 300 | s | The longest walk between two stops in a change, in seconds (300 s is 400 m). | An assumption; no published source. |
| `stop_walk_snap_m` | 300 | m | The farthest a stop may be from the walk layer's nearest node, in metres, to be reached on foot; a stop farther away is treated as outside the study area. | An assumption: the layers' nodes are junctions, so a stop mid-block can be half a block from the nearest. |
| `stop_transfer_s` | 0 | s | The time a transfer at a stop takes between its access points (walk, bike and platform), in seconds. | Zero by construction: the walk to the platform is the walk leg's, and the margin before boarding is `board_slack_s`. |
| `bus_dwell_s` | 20 | s | How long a bus stays at each stop, in seconds; a dwelling bus does not block the traffic behind it. | An assumption standing for a typical stop: a bus's dwell depends mostly on its boardings and alightings (Dueker et al. 2004, Journal of Public Transportation 7(1) 21–40, https://doi.org/10.5038/2375-0901.7.1.2). |
| `bus_pcu` | 2 | PCU | How many passenger car units a bus counts for on the roads. | An assumption; no published source. |
| `bus_plausibility_ratio` | 1.6 | — | A bus pattern whose free-flow time on the roads, stop to stop, exceeds its scheduled time by more than this factor runs by the schedule instead of on the roads. | An assumption; no published source. |
| `bus_stop_snap_m` | 300 | m | The farthest a bus stop may be from the road network's nearest node, in metres, for its buses to ride the roads; a pattern with a stop farther away runs by the schedule. | An assumption, as for `stop_walk_snap_m`. |

## `parking`

Overridden through `parking_options`.

| Name | Default | Unit | Meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `walk_max_s` | 300 | s | The longest walk from a parking to a stop, in seconds (300 s is 400 m); a parking with no stop within it is left out. | An assumption, the same as the longest walk between stops. |
| `reach_car_s` | 1800 | s | The longest drive to a park-and-ride car park, in seconds. | An assumption: 30 minutes; no published drive-time catchment was found. |
| `reach_bike_s` | 1200 | s | The longest ride to a bike parking for bike-and-ride, in seconds of the bike layer's cost (its time with the mixed-traffic and lane factors). | An assumption: 20 minutes; most bike-and-ride users ride 2–5 km to their stop (Martens 2004, Transportation Research Part D 9(4) 281–294, https://www.worldtransitresearch.info/research/2043). |
| `candidates` | 3 | count | How many parkings a park-and-ride or bike-and-ride trip weighs: this many best by an estimate of the whole trip, and this many nearest by drive or ride time, so up to twice as many are tried. | A resource limit, and an assumption about how many stations a traveller weighs. |
| `rank_speed_km_h` | 30 | km/h | The speed, in km/h, a candidate parking's remaining straight-line distance to the destination is divided by to estimate the whole trip and rank candidates before they are tried. | A ranking device, not behaviour: about a tram's or a train's average speed. |
| `floor_car_s` | 120 | s | The time to park a car and walk out of the car park when there is room, in seconds; also the time to fetch it. The time to park is floor + slope × (1 − availability). | An assumption; no published source. |
| `slope_car_s` | 600 | s | The time a car park full for a whole time bin adds to parking, in seconds (linear in the share of the bin it was full). Choice sees the availability expected from the iterations so far; a traveller pays the realised one. | An assumption: searching for a space, which studies of cruising for kerb parking put at several minutes (reviewed by Shoup 2006, Transport Policy 13(6) 479–486, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tranpol.2006.05.005). |
| `floor_bike_s` | 30 | s | The time to park a bike and walk out when there is room, in seconds; also the time to fetch it. | An assumption; no published source. |
| `slope_bike_s` | 180 | s | The time a bike parking full for a whole time bin adds to parking, in seconds. | An assumption; no published source. |
| `snap_m` | 300 | m | The farthest a parking may be from its layers' nearest node, in metres. | An assumption, as for a stop. |
| `bin_s` | 900 | s | The length of the time bins, in seconds, in which each parking's availability is measured (and `parking_bins.parquet` is written). | A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed. |
| `pr_min_km` | 3 | km | The shortest trip, in km as the crow flies, that mode choice offers park-and-ride and bike-and-ride to; a trip given one of those modes takes it at any length. | For computation, and an assumption: nobody drives to a car park for a 1 km trip. Uncalibrated. |
| `reach_car_step_s` | 0 | s | For computation: 0 searches each park-and-ride trip's drive to the car parks at its own departure; above 0, trips leaving one road node within one step of this many seconds share one search made at the step's middle, each drive still timed at its own departure. Approximate. | A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed. |

|---|---|---|---|---|
| `car_eur_km` | 0 | EUR/km | What driving costs per km, in euros: the fuel a driver pays (`cost_running_eur` of a car leg). Weighed only by a choice model that reads money (`beta_cost_eur`). | Uncalibrated: 0, since having a car is access, which traveller classes give. Set your own to weigh fuel. |
| `bike_eur_km` | 0 | EUR/km | What riding one's own bike costs per km, in euros (`cost_running_eur` of a bike leg). | Uncalibrated: nothing, as most models assume. |
| `fare_base_eur` | 0 | EUR | A transit journey's fare, once per journey, in euros (part of `cost_fare_eur`). | Uncalibrated: 0, since holding a pass or paying the fare is access, which traveller classes give. A city's own, to weigh fares: a single ticket in Paris is 2.55 € in 2026 (https://www.iledefrance-mobilites.fr/tarifs-titre-de-transport-en-commun-2026), in Lyon 2.10 € in 2025 (https://www.lebonbon.fr/lyon/news/augmentation-prix-tcl-1er-janvier-2025/); Amsterdam's GVB charges 1.16 € plus 0.217 € per km in 2026 (Vervoerregio Amsterdam, note BBV/2025/15361, p. 2, https://vervoerregio.bestuurlijkeinformatie.nl/Document/View/abddeeb0-be54-4eae-9622-4ac0935df151). |
| `fare_km_eur` | 0 | EUR/km | A transit journey's fare per km ridden, in euros per km, the km counted from each boarding stop to its alighting stop as the crow flies. | Uncalibrated: 0, a flat fare. |
| `fare_transfer_eur` | 0 | EUR | A transit journey's fare per transfer, in euros (a new ticket at each boarding: set it to the base fare). | Uncalibrated: 0, transfers free within a journey. |
| `parking_car_eur` | 0 | EUR | A car park's fee per stay, in euros, where its parking table gives none; counted on the park-and-ride trip that parks, not on the one that fetches. | Uncalibrated: free. |
| `parking_bike_eur` | 0 | EUR | A bike parking's fee per stay, in euros, where its parking table gives none. | Uncalibrated: free. |

## `equilibration.free_flow`

Overridden through `equilibration_options`.

| Name | Default | Unit | Meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `increments` | 5 | count | In how many groups of about equal size, a draw per traveller, the free-flow loading (iteration 0) is built up: the first group chooses on free-flow times, each next one on the times of a loading of the groups before it, until everyone has chosen. 1 lets everyone choose at once on free-flow times. No effect at flow level 0. *(1 at flow_level 0 whatever is set)* | Uncalibrated: groups of a fifth of the travellers (incremental assignment); 5 when not given |
| `warmup` | 1 | count | How many of the first loadings, the free-flow loading's groups included, use the point-queue model, which cannot gridlock, in place of the run's flow level. The last loading of a run that iterates always uses the run's flow level. | A setting: 1 when not given. |

## `equilibration.msa`

Overridden through `equilibration_options`.

| Name | Default | Unit | Meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cost_bin_s` | 300 | s | The length, in seconds, of the time bins in which link times are recorded for the next choice; shorter follows a queue more closely and takes more memory. | A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed. |
| `gap_sample` | 300 | count | How many trips are tested against the whole network (a fastest-route search at the last loading's times) at the last iteration, for the network gap; 0 for none. | A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed. |
| `gap_tolerance` | 0.05 | — | Stop iterating once the disequilibrium (the gap less what the choice model itself expects; the worse of the routes' and the itinerary trips'), averaged over the last three iterations, is below this share, and only from the fourth loading on; 0 never stops early. From 0 to 1. | Uncalibrated: 0.05 is the convergence verdict's "good" (0.15 "acceptable"). |
| `increments` | 5 | count | In how many groups of about equal size, a draw per traveller, the free-flow loading (iteration 0) is built up: the first group chooses on free-flow times, each next one on the times of a loading of the groups before it, until everyone has chosen. 1 lets everyone choose at once on free-flow times. No effect at flow level 0. *(1 at flow_level 0 whatever is set)* | Uncalibrated: groups of a fifth of the travellers (incremental assignment); 5 when not given |
| `itinerary_gap_sample` | 100 000 000 | count | How many transit, park-and-ride and bike-and-ride trips, besides those choosing again, plan their whole choice set after each loading to measure the itinerary gap; the default, 100 000 000, means every trip. Fewer is faster but makes the gap before the last iteration read low; the last iteration always plans every trip. | A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed. |
| `iterations` | 10 | count | The most loadings an `msa` run makes; it may stop earlier at `gap_tolerance`. At iteration i a share 1 / (i + 1) of the travellers, a draw per traveller, chooses again on the last loading's times. | A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed. |
| `route_growth_tolerance` | 1 | — | A run may stop at `gap_tolerance` only while the last route update added routes for at most this share of the pairs it searched; 1 lets the gap alone decide. From 0 to 1. | A setting: 1 when not given; 0 stops no run while the update adds any route. |
| `warmup` | 1 | count | How many of the first loadings, the free-flow loading's groups included, use the point-queue model, which cannot gridlock, in place of the run's flow level. The last loading of a run that iterates always uses the run's flow level. | A setting: 1 when not given. |

## `route_method.penalty`

Overridden through `route_options`.

| Name | Default | Unit | Meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `max_attempts` | 15 | count | The most searches for one origin–destination pair. Given `max_paths` alone, it becomes 3 × `max_paths`. | A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed. |
| `max_detour` | 1.3 | — | No route kept costs more than this multiple of the pair's best route's free-flow cost (at least 1). | An assumption; no published source. |
| `max_overlap` | 0.75 | — | A new route is kept only if it shares at most this share of its cost with each route kept before (above 0, at most 1). | An assumption; no published source. |
| `max_paths` | 5 | count | The most routes kept for one pair (1 to 32). | An assumption; no published source. |
| `penalty` | 1.5 | — | The factor the cost of the links of the route just found is multiplied by before searching again (above 1): larger pushes the next route further from the last. | An assumption; no published source. |

## `route_method.montecarlo`

Overridden through `route_options`.

| Name | Default | Unit | Meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `biased` | 1 | 0 or 1 | 1: a draw raises a link's cost in proportion to its propensity to congest, from the demand (the busiest half-hour's load on free-flow shortest routes over the link's capacity, clipped at 1); 0: every link alike. | A modelling choice: the simulation approach to choice-set generation with its noise where the demand is heavy. Unbiased noise measured worse on the one heavy load it was tried on. |
| `draws` | 16 | count | How many random cost draws to try for one pair (0 to 1 000). | A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed. |
| `max_detour` | 2 | — | No route kept costs more than this multiple of the pair's best route's free-flow cost (at least 1). | An assumption; no published source. |
| `max_overlap` | 0.9 | — | A new route is kept only if it shares at most this share of its cost with each route kept before (above 0, at most 1). | An assumption; no published source. |
| `max_paths` | 10 | count | The most routes kept for one pair (1 to 32). | An assumption; no published source. |
| `seed` | 0 | count | Which draws are made: another value gives another set of draws for every pair. Independent of `master_seed`. | A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed. |
| `sigma` | 4 | — | How far a link's cost may rise in a draw: it is multiplied by 1 + sigma × u × bias, u a uniform draw from 0 to 1 (above 0). | An assumption; no published source. |

## `route_update.best_response`

Overridden through `route_update_options`.

| Name | Default | Unit | Meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `max_routes` | 10 | count | The most routes a pair's set may hold (1 to 32). A full set is still searched: a route at least one second faster than the set's best replaces a route nobody chose in the last choice (never the free-flow shortest one); if every route is in use, it waits. | A setting: a set holds more routes than a traveller is offered (`choice_max_routes`). |
| `searches` | 1 | count | How many fastest-route searches per pair per iteration, at evenly spread quantiles of the pair's departures (1: the median). More finds routes that pay only at some hours, and makes bigger sets. | A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed. |
| `slack` | 0.02 | — | A pair is not searched while its set's best route at its departure is within this share of the route's free-flow time, since no route is faster than free flow: the regret left is at most this share. 0 searches every pair. From 0 to 1. | A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed. |
| `tree_step_s` | 0 | s | Search trees: 0 searches each pair on its own, at its departures; above 0, departures are rounded to this step (in seconds) and the pairs of one origin at one rounded departure share one search tree, which finds each one's fastest route at once. Approximate (the routes are the fastest at the rounded departure) and much faster where many trips share an origin; the starter cases use 1 800. | A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed. |

## `choice_model.logit`

Overridden through `choice_options`.

| Name | Default | Unit | Meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `beta_bike_mixed_km` | -0.16 | per km | Weighs each km of a bike leg in mixed traffic, on top of its time, so a ride's route and its mode are chosen alike: at −0.16 it matches the bike route search's mixed-traffic factor (1.2) at the default time weight and bike speed. | An assumption, derived from the bike route search's defaults (0.8 minute more per km at 15 km/h, times −0.2). |
| `beta_cost_eur` | -1.2 | per EUR | Weighs what an alternative costs, per euro (`cost_eur`). A value of time of V euros per hour is `beta_cost_eur = beta_time_min × 60 / V`; every shipped price is 0, so money weighs only the prices a scenario gives. | An assumption: a value of time of 10 € per hour at the default time weight. |
| `beta_ln_path_size` | 1 | per unit of the attribute | Weighs the logarithm of the path-size factor: routes that share links with the others in the set split their share, which repairs the logit's blindness to overlap (the path-size logit). | The path-size term of Ben-Akiva and Bierlaire (1999) |
| `beta_time_min` | -0.2 | per min | Weighs the expected travel time, per minute (door to door for an itinerary): the main term of the utility. At −0.2 a route four minutes slower is taken with about 45 % of the weight of one that is not. | An assumption, not a calibration. |
| `beta_transfers` | -1 | per unit of the attribute | Weighs each change of vehicle, per transfer: −1 is about five minutes of riding at the default time weight. | An assumption, well below the 15.2–17.7 minutes of riding Garcia-Martinez et al. (2018), Transportation Research Part A 114 52–66, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tra.2018.01.016, estimate in Madrid. |
| `beta_wait_min` | -0.09 | per min | Weighs minutes waiting at stops on top of `time_min`, so a minute waited weighs about 1.45 times a minute riding at the default time weight. | Wardman (2004), Transport Policy 11(4) 363–377, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tranpol.2004.05.001: waiting weighs on average 1.47 times in-vehicle time. |
| `beta_walk_min` | -0.13 | per min | Weighs minutes walking on top of `time_min`, so a minute walked weighs about 1.65 times a minute riding at the default time weight. 0 for a car route. | Wardman (2004), Transport Policy 11(4) 363–377, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tranpol.2004.05.001: walking weighs on average 1.66 times in-vehicle time in British evidence (which the author finds too low). |
| `beta_length_km` | 0 | per km | Weighs a route's length in km (an itinerary's car or bike leg's), per km. *(0 unless set)* | No default weight: 0 leaves the attribute out of the utility. |
| `beta_detour` | 0 | per unit of the attribute | Weighs an alternative's time over the best alternative's, minus one, per unit. *(0 unless set)* | No default weight: 0 leaves the attribute out of the utility. |
| `beta_overlap` | 0 | per unit of the attribute | Weighs a route's largest share of its cost shared with an earlier route of its set (0 for an itinerary), per unit. *(0 unless set)* | No default weight: 0 leaves the attribute out of the utility. |
| `beta_n_links` | 0 | per unit of the attribute | Weighs a route's number of links (an itinerary's car or bike leg's), per unit. *(0 unless set)* | No default weight: 0 leaves the attribute out of the utility. |
| `beta_car_min` | 0 | per min | Weighs minutes driving: the car's part of the time, per minute. *(0 unless set)* | No default weight: 0 leaves the attribute out of the utility. |
| `beta_bike_min` | 0 | per min | Weighs minutes riding a bike: the bike's part of the time, per minute. *(0 unless set)* | No default weight: 0 leaves the attribute out of the utility. |
| `beta_ride_min` | 0 | per min | Weighs minutes on board transit vehicles, per minute. *(0 unless set)* | No default weight: 0 leaves the attribute out of the utility. |
| `beta_parking_min` | 0 | per min | Weighs minutes parking or fetching a car or bike, per minute. *(0 unless set)* | No default weight: 0 leaves the attribute out of the utility. |
| `beta_bike_separated_km` | 0 | per km | Weighs the bike leg's km on separate tracks, per km. *(0 unless set)* | No default weight: 0 leaves the attribute out of the utility. |
| `beta_bike_lane_km` | 0 | per km | Weighs the bike leg's km on painted lanes or cycle streets, per km. *(0 unless set)* | No default weight: 0 leaves the attribute out of the utility. |
| `beta_walk_access_min` | 0 | per min | Weighs minutes walking to the first stop (part of `walk_min`), per minute. A part is weighed on top of its total's coefficient, or instead of it. *(0 unless set)* | No default weight: 0 leaves the attribute out of the utility. |
| `beta_walk_egress_min` | 0 | per min | Weighs minutes walking from the last stop (part of `walk_min`), per minute. A part is weighed on top of its total's coefficient, or instead of it. *(0 unless set)* | No default weight: 0 leaves the attribute out of the utility. |
| `beta_walk_transfer_min` | 0 | per min | Weighs minutes walking between stops (part of `walk_min`), per minute. A part is weighed on top of its total's coefficient, or instead of it. *(0 unless set)* | No default weight: 0 leaves the attribute out of the utility. |
| `beta_wait_first_min` | 0 | per min | Weighs minutes waiting at the first stop (part of `wait_min`), per minute. A part is weighed on top of its total's coefficient, or instead of it. *(0 unless set)* | No default weight: 0 leaves the attribute out of the utility. |

| `beta_cost_fare_eur` | 0 | per EUR | Weighs a transit journey's fare, in euros, per euro. *(0 unless set)* | No default weight: 0 leaves the attribute out of the utility. |
| `beta_trip_departure_h` | 0 | per unit of the attribute | Weighs the trip's departure in hours after midnight. Being the same for every alternative of a choice, it changes no probability on its own; it weighs in a product with another attribute, `beta_<a>*<b>`. *(0 unless set)* | No default weight: 0 leaves the attribute out of the utility. |

| `beta_mode_transit` | 0 | per unit of the attribute | The constant of the `transit` mode: weighs the attribute that is 1 for a transit alternative, 0 otherwise.
